=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:548-599 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_is_release_entry` uses `RELEASE_CONDITION_RE.match(dormant) or RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE.match(title)`, so a real human step whose title starts with a release verb and mentions "stable" within 200 characters (e.g. "Sync the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret to the stable environment" with dormant_until `DEPLOY_TOKEN`) counts as a release entry.
  WHY: Once compare/<sha>...stable returns ahead or identical, resolve() hands the entry to `_render_resolved`, which ticks every `- [ ]` box including the human step and can close the tracker as completed; this breaks the documented "never ticked" contract, and the SECRET_STEP fixture hides the bug because its title starts with "Add". All reviewers agree on the severity (MAJOR).
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:391-439,717-735 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: resolve()'s last re-read of comments (lines 717-720) is not atomic with its close comment and `state=closed` PATCH (lines 731-732), and upsert() (lists open trackers at line 391, loads comments at line 420, posts at line 439) never re-checks the tracker's state after posting, so an entry posted concurrently can land on a tracker that resolve then closes.
  WHY: Later resolve, tick and upsert runs list only `state=open` trackers, so the stranded entry's unticked human step is never processed and the next upsert creates a second tracker; upsert still reports success. The existing test covers only the first-read window. All reviewers agree on the severity (MAJOR).
- tests/test_operator_step_issue.py:52-67 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new FakeGitHub `state=closed` PATCH branch runs before the existing PATCH handler and removes the target issue from `self.issues`, whereas the old generic branch only rewrote `issue["body"]`; this changes listing results for digest paths that close an issue (scripts/operator_step_issue.py:964 and :1081).
  WHY: The pre-push gate attributes 10 needs-human digest test failures to this change (e.g. test_needs_human_digest_park_reports_the_park_when_the_post_create_listing_fails, test_operator_step_tick_without_a_tracker_writes_nothing_and_ignores_the_digest). z-ai_glm-5_3-flash notes that this does not explain all ten failures. Severity: MAJOR from z-ai_glm-5_3-flash; minimax_minimax-m3 stated none.

  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]

  WHY: The changes are not verified and fail CI, which makes the PR unmergeable. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash also notes that the three test_activation_verify.py done-checks are `unmet`; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 says those tests exist in the diff and "unmet" means the gate did not run them.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:PR body and commit messages | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Auto-close keywords reference orchestrator-tracking issue #2734.
  WHY: On merge GitHub would auto-close tracking issue #2734 and stop orchestrator wave dispatch for the project. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes this: it says the #2734 lint lines are fixture output from test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py, and that the PR body uses `Closes .../issues/9203` and `Refs #8291`.
- PR body and branch commit history (check-run `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, run 43042064535, job 130596182541, head 8b0cb63e0e72788310f0f2145181715ace79cedf):`scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` output in the job log; PR body line 1 and commit message #2 line 3 (`though each conflict was resolved: #2734 failed`) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The required check fails on auto-close keyword violations against `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issue #2734: `Fixes #2734` in the PR body, and the keyword `resolved` followed by `#2734` in an existing branch commit.
  WHY: Per CLAUDE.md §19/§21, merging would auto-close tracking issue #2734 and stop wave dispatch; CI cannot go green until the PR body uses `Refs #` and commit #2 is reworded (rebase plus force-push). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes this attribution (it calls it fixture output, severity NIT).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:543,813 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The required check tests-hooks-and-orchestrator fails on head 8b0cb63 for a reason this reviewer cannot map to any hunk in the PR; none of the 10 PR files runs in that job, and the `##[error][lint_pr_body_auto_close] ... #2734` lines are fixture output from test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py.
  WHY: The check stays red for a reason outside this diff, so the editor should check whether the failure is inherited from the base (the pre-push gate lists 33 inherited failures) before changing PR files; the pass-1 BLOCKER about rewording the PR body or commits for #2734 is not supported by the evidence. === FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE at lines 548-552; _is_release_entry at lines 594-599: `RELEASE_CONDITION_RE.match(dormant) or RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE.match(title)` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A matching title makes a step count as a release step even when its own dormant line names something else (e.g. "Sync the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret to the stable environment" with `Stays off until then: `DEPLOY_TOKEN`.`).
  WHY: resolve() (lines 643 onward) lets the entry through the not_release gate, and `_render_resolved` ticks every box and may close the tracker, which breaks the "never ticked" contract. SECRET_STEP passes only because its title starts with "Add". Proposed fix: `RELEASE_CONDITION_RE.match(dormant) or (not dormant and RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE.match(title))`.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:resolve() close path, lines 718-735 (recheck `load_entry_comments`, then the PATCH `state=closed` at line 732); upsert(), lines 391-439 (lists open trackers, reads comments, posts the entry comment at line 439) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: resolve's last re-read is not atomic with its close PATCH, and upsert never checks the tracker's state after posting, so an entry can land on a closed tracker while upsert returns success.
  WHY: Later runs list only `state=open` trackers, so the stranded human step is never shown again and the next upsert creates a new tracker. Proposed fix: upsert re-reads the tracker after posting and re-posts or reopens it if closed.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:job `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` (line 543); the step at line 813 runs tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The required check fails on head 8b0cb63 for a reason that cannot be mapped to any PR hunk; the #2734 lint lines are fixture output, and the PR body uses `Closes .../issues/9203` and `Refs #8291`.
  WHY: The check stays red for a reason outside this diff; the editor should check whether the failure is inherited from the base (33 inherited failures) before changing PR files. The pass-1 #2734 BLOCKER is unsupported.
- IMPLICIT-EXECUTION: NONE. The orchestrate_poll.yml step (lines 329-352) is safely gated: symlink and marker checks, `continue-on-error: true`, a kill switch, and a trusted PAT login.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. Every P10 deliverable has a hunk, and the three "unmet" acceptance tests exist in tests/test_activation_verify.py. The pass-1 scope-violation TASK_GAPs (clarify.yml, plan.yml, run_plan_codex.sh, stage_support_for_phase.sh, the p2b agents fragment) are rejected as base-branch content (scripts/run_plan_codex.sh line 7, lines 311-312, 349, 364, 638-646).
